text: The treatment records the NLEADS result on POST /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result with the legacy CreditResult body, and the integration-base operation of the same suffix calls it.
why: TSD S2 T-A.1 carries no credit-result operation, and the legacy contract and the Ownership Map keep that suffix on the integration base.
read: The suffix is copied from the legacy contract on the owning service's base (DP-13); a 200 with the Treatment and the same error set as API-S2-003.
confirm: Solution architect and the API Specification v5 owner
impact: None on other services: the integration base keeps its own operation and calls this one.

text: The record state column of treatment carries SUBMITTED, APPROVED and REFUSED for a credit result, and no list of values is added to the data model by this story.
why: Legacy section 9 names the three states, while TSD S2 T3.2 gives no list for the record state and T3.0 fixes only state varchar(40).
read: The values are written as record lifecycle states of the row; a later data-model issue turns them into a list without a code change.
confirm: Business analyst, S2, and the data model owner
impact: A reporting query on the treatment state reads the same three strings in every environment.

text: The reference lists of rwb-case and the authorise answer of rwb-access are consumed as published contracts, and the text of MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-GEN-006 stays as the placeholder of section 14.
why: Neither TSD S2 nor the legacy story states the paths, the parameters or the answer shapes, and the legacy message table has no text for those three messages.
read: One hop, 2 s timeout and a fake per contract; the message identifiers are cited from legacy section 12 and their texts are not invented.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-case and rwb-access contract owners
impact: No behaviour depends on the wording of a refusal message.

text: The migration of this story adds the check credit_result_reason is not null when credit_result = 'REFUSED' in rwb_treatment.
why: TSD S2 T3.1 marks all four columns not required and states no rule between the result and the reason, while the legacy solution plan requires the check.
read: The four columns are added free of null; the check protects the refusal path at the schema, not only in the service.
impact: A refusal without a reason cannot be stored by any path, including a batch fix.

text: nleads_ref is validated as 1 to 30 characters of letters, digits and dashes, held as a reference row so a confirmed format is a configuration change.
why: The legacy contract records the format as assumed until SCB IT confirms it under DL12, and TSD S2 gives only varchar(30).
read: The same limit as the physical type; the pattern is a data row and not a constant in code.
confirm: SCB IT, with the business analyst of S2
impact: A confirmed NLEADS format needs no code change and no migration.

text: The comparison of the level NLEADS returned with the level the delegation of authority requires is performed by the rwb-decision slice and by the caller slice, not here; this service stores the level as recorded and validates only list membership.
why: The legacy story refuses a level below the requirement on the same endpoint, while the target puts the delegation table and the comparison with rwb-decision and keeps the case state with rwb-case.
read: The treatment records what NLEADS decided and refuses only a value outside LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL; the legacy AC7 is proved in RWB-P7-E2006-APP.
confirm: Business analyst, S2, and the rwb-decision owner
impact: A result refused for its level never reaches this service, so no row is written.

text: The dependency rows of the metadata stay as the work package fixes them (None) while the pattern table lists the four platform contracts the DP table adds.
why: The work package fixes the four dependency rows as empty; Template and Rules R5.5 adds a platform contract for each of DP-03, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19.
read: The story is Day 1 and builds against the platform fakes; the lane group is the contract group of wave 2.
confirm: Delivery lead, when the platform CON stories are numbered
impact: The lane may be restated by the assembler; no build order changes.

text: The credit result is shown read only on the SCR-14 treatment panel with no layout or masking decision taken by this story.
why: Legacy section 15 names the screen and its two states and the screen inventory gives no field list, layout or masking rule for the five values.
read: The panel reads the extended treatment read; the design work fixes the layout and changes no contract.
confirm: UX lead, with the business analyst of S2
impact: No field of the answer is removed by the design; the four values and the state stay on the read.

text: Service facts for this story are taken from the service note of FSD S2 v4 and the T0 sections of TSD S2 v3, because the context pack and the S2 extracts named by the work package are not present in this workspace.
why: _work/msr/context/S2.md and the _work/msr/extract files of the FSD and TSD folders do not exist at the time of the run.
read: The service row, the schema, the base, the topic, the queue, the Java package, the lists of values and the ownership rows are read from those two documents, which cite Arch v5 slides 41 and 42.
confirm: Coordinator, when the context pack is issued
impact: If the pack differs on a service fact, only the identifiers of section 12 change; no criterion changes.

text: No human approval of this story is recorded; it is issued in Draft status under the D-RCV-60 realignment.
why: The realignment run proceeds without a human approval gate and the story has no approved status in any source.
read: Status is Draft (realignment v1) and the story is buildable on its fakes as soon as the platform contracts are published.
confirm: Delivery lead, at the next approval gate
impact: None on the content; the approval is recorded later.
